subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Should this issue stay open as the umbrella for the remaining healthy-vLLM timeout and gateway latency cascade until a current-main live trace isolates it, or should maintainers split/redirect the remaining slices to narrower issues?
rationale: The report spans provider timeouts, fallback classification, cron/live-session behavior, provider-auth startup, and gateway RPC latency; current main fixes several slices but does not prove the remaining central behavior is gone or identify one safe repair boundary.

options.title: Keep umbrella pending live trace
options.body: Leave this issue open and require a current-main local vLLM trace before queueing a new fix, while using narrower sibling issues only for clearly isolated slices.

options.title: Split to sibling issues
options.body: Move remaining timeout, provider-auth, and stall-recovery questions into narrower canonical issues and close this only after those links preserve the reporter evidence.

options.title: Sponsor a focused reproduction PR
options.body: Have a maintainer own a live repro harness or diagnostic logging PR first, without changing timeout or fallback policy yet.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella pending live trace
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open and require a current-main local vLLM trace before queueing a new fix, while using narrower sibling issues only for clearly isolated slices.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the current assignee and already acted on the adjacent provider-auth startup fix path.
